A curious spotted fawn watches from the ferns at the edge of the glade, perfectly still and unafraid.
A tiny carved door, no bigger than a book, is set into the mossy roots of an ancient oak.
A white stag stands motionless among the distant silver birches, its great antlers catching the moonlight.
A sleeping hedgehog lies curled on the flat crown of a toadstool, breathing softly in the quiet air.
A ring of tiny dancing lights drifts just above the grass, spinning in a slow and patient circle.
A fox sits among the roots of a fallen tree, watching with amber eyes that hold an old knowledge.
A snail makes its unhurried way across a leaf that glows faintly green from somewhere deep within.
A tiny wooden boat, perfectly made, bobs gently on the still pool, tied to a reed with silver thread.
A bird lands on a low branch, and its feathers catch the light like scattered sapphires and garnets.
A face is carved into a mossy stone, half-swallowed by ivy, its expression patient and almost amused.
A trail of tiny footprints crosses the soft mud at the water's edge and disappears into the reeds.
A single flower grows apart from the others, its petals holding a steady, sourceless golden glow.
A moth rests on the bark of an elder tree, its wings dusted with something that shimmers like frost.
A small lantern hangs from a low branch, no taller than a thimble, burning with a steady warm flame.
A badger ambles slowly through the bracken at dusk, a crown of woven flowers sitting crooked on its head.
Three acorn caps are arranged in a precise triangle on a flat stone, as though set there with great care.
A spider has spun its web between two hawthorn branches and threaded it, somehow, with tiny drops of amber.
A low hum drifts through the air near the old standing stone, felt more in the chest than truly heard.
A pair of tiny shoes, no longer than a finger, sits neatly outside the small door in the tree root.
A crow perches on the gate post and tilts its head, as if it has been waiting specifically for you.
A cluster of mushrooms grows in a perfect ring, the grass inside it greener and softer than anywhere else.
A dragonfly hovers above the pool, its wings catching every colour of the late afternoon in quick succession.
A bundle of dried herbs and river-smoothed pebbles is tucked into the hollow of a stone wall, carefully arranged.
A frog sits at the edge of the pool wearing, improbably, a tiny collar of woven watercress and river pearls.
The old willow at the water's edge has a hollow just large enough to look into, and inside it glows.
